subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the stray SDK export is removed, should OpenClaw accept the `@microsoft/mxc-sdk` / `node-pty` native dependency graph and the SDK's argv-carried base64 config boundary for a first-party external MXC sandbox plugin?
rationale: The remaining non-mechanical decision is a sandbox/security and supply-chain boundary: the plugin is useful and well-proven, but it introduces native executables, install scripts, and an upstream config transport that green CI cannot approve by policy.

options.title: Accept With Exact-Head Approval
options.body: Approve the native dependency graph and SDK argv boundary for the final head after the public SDK export is removed and dependency-guard is explicitly authorized.

options.title: Pause For Upstream Transport
options.body: Hold the PR until MXC provides a non-argv config transport or clearer security guidance for sensitive sandbox policy fields.

options.title: Move Out Of First-Party Track
options.body: Decline first-party packaging for now and ask for an external ClawHub/plugin experiment that does not require OpenClaw dependency graph approval.

recommendation.title: Accept With Exact-Head Approval
recommendation.body: Approve the native dependency graph and SDK argv boundary for the final head after the public SDK export is removed and dependency-guard is explicitly authorized.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the current assignee and has recent sandbox/plugin SDK history; secops still needs to approve the dependency graph separately.
